headline: High: CrewAI’s default shell/network/file access can cascade into Great Expectations workflows, creating medium-to-high risks for prompt injection, leakage, and compliance when they share data or workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host filesystem, run browsers, and use stdin/stdout; Great Expectations reads data sources and writes validation results/documentation. If CrewAI places attacker-controlled content into shared files, Great Expectations may ingest it as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes untrusted content into a directory Great Expectations later reads
IF Great Expectations parses file contents as authoritative configuration or documentation
mitigations: Separate working directories for the two agents
Add a manual review step before Great Expectations consumes CrewAI-produced files
Use read-only mounts for Great Expectations inputs
Strip instructions-like text from shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on exchanged files

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and handles API keys, while Great Expectations processes data sources, validation results, and documentation. A shared workspace or copied files could expose sensitive inputs or outputs across the pair. Because no direct shared-storage mechanism is documented, this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or data directory
IF CrewAI writes crew data or secrets into files Great Expectations can read
mitigations: Use separate directories and credentials
Exclude secrets from any shared artifacts
Restrict Great Expectations to sanitized sample data
Rotate any API keys that may have been written to disk
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress; Great Expectations can install packages and read/write data-related files. Overlapping writes to the same workspace can corrupt artifacts or overwrite validation outputs. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so the conflict is real in default shared-workspace setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF CrewAI subprocesses and Great Expectations jobs run concurrently
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared outputs
Run one agent at a time for mutable artifacts
Back up the workspace before execution
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, and Great Expectations produces validation results and documentation. If CrewAI-generated outputs are treated as inputs or facts by Great Expectations without verification, errors can propagate into reports or downstream actions. Because the pair lacks documented verification boundaries, I escalate to high.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes CrewAI-produced artifacts without independent validation
IF CrewAI outputs are used to generate validation documentation or decisions
mitigations: Require human review of CrewAI outputs before ingestion
Compare outputs against source data before reporting
Keep validation logic separate from narrative generation
Log provenance for every imported artifact
requires-engineering: add schema and content verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Great Expectations processes data sources, validation results, and documentation. If regulated data is placed into CrewAI and then copied into Great Expectations outputs or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so the safest supported rating is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in crew inputs or validation datasets
IF either agent logs or retains those artifacts longer than policy allows
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Minimize logging of inputs and outputs
Set short retention on validation artifacts
Review where files are stored and backed up
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
